title: Ordinary left Kan image of the presheaf bar complex and comma-chain reindexing
statement:
Let $u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ be a functor of small categories in [def-weil-size-convention], with the topology generated by singleton identity coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Fix a commutative ring $R$ and write $\mathcal A_{\mathcal C}=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{op},\operatorname{Mod}_R)$ for module presheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $g^{-1}$ be precomposition with $u$ and $g_!=\operatorname{Lan}_{u^{op}}$ its left adjoint. Use the canonical everywhere-defined total left derived functor $Lg_!$, comparison $\varepsilon_C:Lg_!QC\to Qg_!C$ and normalized adjunction of [lem-trf-continuous-cocontinuous-derived-shriek], with $Q$ the localization of complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $F\in\mathcal A_{\mathcal E}$, use the specific augmented complex $B(F)$ of [lem-trf-augmented-presheaf-bar-resolution] and the canonical ordinary Kan isomorphisms of [lem-trf-representable-sum-shriek-acyclic]. For $V\in\mathcal D$ let $\mathcal I_V=(V\downarrow u)$ have objects $(U,t:V\to uU)$ and arrows $h:(U,t)\to(U',t')$ with $u(h)t=t'$. Define $F_V(U,t)=F(U)$ and restriction $F_V(h)=F(h)$. Let $K_{\mathcal I_V}(F_V)$ be the category bar complex of [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar]. There is an isomorphism in $D(R)$
$$Q((g_!B(F))(V))\xrightarrow\sim QK_{\mathcal I_V}(F_V),$$
represented by a specified isomorphism of cochain complexes $\beta_{F,V}$. In degree $-n$, it sends $(t:V\to uU_n,U_n\xrightarrow{h_n}\cdots\xrightarrow{h_1}U_0,x)$ to $((U_n,t_n)\to\cdots\to(U_0,t_0),x)$, where $t_n=t$ and $t_{j-1}=u(h_j)t_j$ for $j=n,\ldots,1$. Its inverse forgets $t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1}$. It intertwines the first face with deletion of $(U_n,t_n)$, each internal face with composition, and the last face with $F(h_1)$, using the same alternating signs.
For $s:V'\to V$, define $\rho_s$ on the comma bar complexes by replacing every $(U_j,t_j)$ with $(U_j,t_js)$ and keeping $x$ fixed. This is a chain map, and
$$\beta_{F,V'}(g_!B(F))(s)=\rho_s\beta_{F,V}.$$
For $q:F\to F'$, define $q_V:F_V\to F'_V$ by $q_{V,(U,t)}=q_U$. Then $\beta_{F',V}(g_!B(q))(V)=K_{\mathcal I_V}(q_V)\beta_{F,V}$. The maps $\rho_s$ preserve identities and compose contravariantly, and commute with coefficient maps: $\rho_sK_{\mathcal I_V}(q_V)=K_{\mathcal I_{V'}}(q_{V'})\rho_s$. These equations hold for the displayed chain maps and hence in $D(R)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-augmented-presheaf-bar-resolution] in degree $-n$ and the ordinary sum formula of [lem-trf-representable-sum-shriek-acyclic]. They identify $(g_!B(F))^{-n}(V)$ with $\bigoplus_{U_n\to\cdots\to U_0}\bigoplus_{t:V\to uU_n}F(U_0)$, and its positive terms with zero. These are small sums: both categories are small in the specified universes. In these coordinates a restriction along $s:V'\to V$ replaces $t$ by $ts$. A coefficient map $q$ acts by $q_{U_0}$ on $x$. The canonical Kan identification is natural. In particular the map $L_U(M)\to L_{U'}(M)$ sending $(a,x)$ to $(ha,x)$, for $h:U\to U'$, becomes the map $L_{uU}(M)\to L_{uU'}(M)$ sending $(t,x)$ to $(u(h)t,x)$. This also follows from the stated identity-summand adjunction formula: the map is determined by the identity generator, whose image is the $h$-summand, and the canonical Kan map sends it to the $u(h)$-summand without changing its coefficient. The hypotheses of [lem-trf-representable-sum-shriek-acyclic] hold here: $u$ preserves the singleton identity coverings and is cocontinuous (the identity cover refines every covering), so $Lg_!$ is the everywhere-defined derived functor with canonical comparison of [lem-trf-continuous-cocontinuous-derived-shriek] fixed in the statement, and [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar], applied to $\mathcal E$ and to $\mathcal D$, gives everywhere-defined total left derived functors of $C_{\mathcal E,R}$ and $C_{\mathcal D,R}$ with their canonical comparisons.

source.place: Tags 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), representable bar terms; 08PH (example-morphism-categories), ordinary functorial maps. Agent expansion for ordinary Kan images.

proof.text: The comma category is small: its objects are pairs from the small object set of $\mathcal E$ and the small hom sets $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(V,uU)$; its arrows are subsets of the hom sets of $\mathcal E$. For an index $(t,U_n\xrightarrow{h_n}\cdots\xrightarrow{h_1}U_0)$ of the preceding sum, set $t_n=t$ and recursively $t_{j-1}=u(h_j)t_j$. Each $h_j$ is then an arrow $(U_j,t_j)\to(U_{j-1},t_{j-1})$ of $\mathcal I_V$. Conversely the defining equation for an arrow of $\mathcal I_V$ forces precisely this recursion, so forgetting $t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1}$ is an inverse on indices. Carry the coefficient $x\in F(U_0)=F_V(U_0,t_0)$ identically along this bijection. Extending by addition gives mutually inverse $R$-linear maps $\beta^{-n}_{F,V}$ and $\gamma^{-n}_{F,V}$ of the direct sums. For $n=0$ this is just $(t,U_0,x)\leftrightarrow((U_0,t),x)$; in positive degrees use the unique maps between zero modules. No choices of extra arrows are required.

source.place: Tag 08PK (lemma-compute-left-derived-g-shriek), definition of the comma category in the proof; explicit index bijection expanding the source.

proof.text: Let $n\ge1$. By the first-face formula of [lem-trf-augmented-presheaf-bar-resolution], and its Kan image computed in step 1 using [lem-trf-representable-sum-shriek-acyclic], $d_0$ replaces $(t,U_n\xrightarrow{h_n}U_{n-1}\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$ by $(u(h_n)t,U_{n-1}\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$. Its new initial arrow is $t_{n-1}$, and the recursion gives exactly the remaining arrows $t_{n-2},\ldots,t_0$. Under $\beta$ this is deletion of $(U_n,t_n)$, which is the first face of [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar] on $\mathcal I_V$. Thus $\beta d_0=d_0\beta$.

For $0<j<n$ put $m=n-j$. Deleting $U_m$ composes $h_mh_{m+1}$; the new comma-arrow equation is $u(h_mh_{m+1})t_{m+1}=u(h_m)u(h_{m+1})t_{m+1}=t_{m-1}$. Hence the internal faces of [lem-trf-augmented-presheaf-bar-resolution] and [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar] agree under $\beta$, with coefficient unchanged. The last face deletes $U_0$ and applies $F(h_1)$ to $x$; in the comma category this is exactly $F_V(h_1)=F(h_1)$, so the last faces also agree. Both complexes use $\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^jd_j$ with this same numbering; adding the face equalities proves $\beta d=d\beta$. Their degree-zero outgoing differentials vanish. Since $\gamma$ is the degreewise inverse, multiplying this equation by the inverses gives $d\gamma=\gamma d$. Thus $\beta$ and $\gamma$ are inverse cochain maps, not just inverse graded maps.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), displayed three-term differential and its general alternating-face convention; Tag 08PK, comma coefficient restrictions.

proof.text: For $s:V'\to V$, $(U,t)\mapsto(U,ts)$ preserves comma arrows since $u(h)(ts)=(u(h)t)s$, and preserves their identities and composition. Replacing all $t_j$ by $t_js$ therefore sends a comma chain to a comma chain. It commutes with deletion and composition of its vertices and with the last restriction $F(h_1)$, which does not depend on $t_j$; by the face formula in [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar], its coefficientwise extension $\rho_s$ is a cochain map. By [lem-trf-representable-sum-shriek-acyclic] the ordinary Kan restriction in step 1 changes $t_n$ to $t_ns$. Its recursively computed arrows are $u(h_j)(t_js)=t_{j-1}s$. Both $\beta_{F,V'}(g_!B(F))(s)$ and $\rho_s\beta_{F,V}$ therefore send the same summand element to the chain $((U_n,t_ns)\to\cdots\to(U_0,t_0s),x)$. The equality on all summands gives the asserted equality of cochain maps.

source.place: Tag 08PK (lemma-compute-left-derived-g-shriek), comma presheaf and restriction maps; Tag 08PH (example-morphism-categories), maps on bar generators.

proof.text: For $q:F\to F'$, the maps $(q_V)_{(U,t)}=q_U$ form a natural transformation because $q_UF(h)=F'(h)q_{U'}$ for $h:U\to U'$. The functorial bar construction of [lem-trf-augmented-presheaf-bar-resolution] applies $q_{U_0}$ to each coefficient, and its ordinary Kan image has the same formula by [lem-trf-representable-sum-shriek-acyclic]. The coefficient-map formula of [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar], specialized to the identity functor of $\mathcal I_V$ and the fixed ring $R$, also applies $q_{U_0}$ and keeps the comma chain fixed. Both $\beta_{F',V}(g_!B(q))(V)$ and $K_{\mathcal I_V}(q_V)\beta_{F,V}$ therefore take $(t,U_\bullet,x)$ to $((U_n,t_n)\to\cdots\to(U_0,t_0),q_{U_0}x)$. This proves the coefficient naturality on cochain maps.

source.place: Tags 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), functoriality in coefficients; 08PH (example-morphism-categories), displayed chain map with coefficient map.

proof.text: For composable $s:V'\to V$ and $s':V''\to V'$, two successive replacements give $(t_js)s'=t_j(ss')$ for every vertex. Thus $\rho_{s'}\rho_s=\rho_{ss'}$, while $\rho_{1_V}=1$. Finally both $\rho_sK_{\mathcal I_V}(q_V)$ and $K_{\mathcal I_{V'}}(q_{V'})\rho_s$ send $(U_\bullet,t_\bullet,x)$ to $(U_\bullet,t_\bullet s,q_{U_0}x)$. These are equal as linear maps on every summand in every degree, and hence as cochain maps.

source.place: Tags 08PH (example-morphism-categories) and 08PK (lemma-compute-left-derived-g-shriek), explicit composition and coefficient checks for the restriction formula.

proof.text: Apply the localization functor $Q$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to the inverse cochain maps of step 4. Functoriality gives $Q\beta\,Q\gamma=1$ and $Q\gamma\,Q\beta=1$, so $Q\beta$ is the required isomorphism in $D(R)$. Applying the same functor to the cochain-map equalities of steps 5--7 proves all the displayed equalities in $D(R)$. This uses only the ordinary Kan image of $B(F)$; no acyclicity of an evaluation functor or derived comparison is needed for this chain-level assertion.

from.place: Proof (1)--(2), semistable-alteration input in the nearby-cycle branch: ILO Exposé X, Theorem 3.4, Step 3, invoking Temkin 2010, Theorems 1.5 and 1.1 for a semistable multipointed modification. Temkin proof component: Marked dualizing line bundle and contracted-component degrees.
